week_overview: Across Week 2’s 15 games, receptions are the busiest market for flagged edges with 465, ahead of receiving yards at 280 and rushing yards at 275. Kalif Raymond’s receptions lead the individual list at 1,497 basis points, with Cooper Rush and Aaron Rodgers passing touchdowns right behind at 1,491 each. Those figures indicate the reported edge sizes, not whether to bet an over or under—the supplied data doesn’t name either side. There are no arbitrage opportunities flagged, so nothing here points to an arbitrage setup worth exploring. With just three plays above the model’s 80% confidence threshold, it’s a week to be selective rather than treat every flag as a strong pick, especially since these model estimates are experimental.

The catch is that these entries don’t identify the stat being measured, so I’d want that clarified before calling any of them a usable pick—especially the opposing 0.5 sides. A positive edge means the model rates the named side above its market probability; it doesn’t mean “bet the over.” These are experimental estimates, not guarantees, and the missing stat labels limit how confidently we can interpret them.

Across the labeled markets, rushing yards lean toward overs, passing attempts and completions lean toward unders, and passing yards are evenly split.
